one_liner: A program coordinator role for George Mason University's ICAP program in Fairfax; the posting gives no duties, so confirm what ICAP is before applying.
fit_summary: Without a description, fit can't be judged well. Daniel's project operations and coordination work at IEM suits a general coordinator role, but if ICAP is an academic, student-services or research program, the fit is weaker.
eligibility: Open the full posting on jobs.virginia.gov or GMU's careers site to confirm who may apply. The summary lists no restrictions.
Check the required qualifications on the full posting for any degree requirement. Many GMU coordinator roles ask for a bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
Confirm whether the job is a classified state, administrative/professional faculty, or wage position. This affects pay, benefits, and how the application is reviewed.
Expect a background check, which is standard for GMU hires.
strategy: Before tailoring anything, get the full description from the jobs.virginia.gov link or GMU's Jobs at Mason site. Find out what ICAP stands for and what the role does.
Frame the IEM work as program and project coordination for government clients. Describe deliverables, deadlines, stakeholder meetings, and reports in concrete terms, without overstating your title.
Lead with your relationship-building and public-facing strengths: coordinating partners, running meetings, and answering inquiries.
If ICAP touches policy, public service, or civic engagement, tie in your knowledge of U.S. politics and policy in a short cover letter.
State resumes are not limited to two pages, but keep yours focused (one to two pages) and use the posting's key terms where they are true. Because the job is open until filled, apply quickly.
The Manassas-to-Fairfax commute is reasonable. Still, ask about on-site expectations, since the posting lists the job as not remote.
resume_bullets: Helped sequence onboarding for FEMA Public Assistance employees by organizing spreadsheets and analyzing the data for decision makers (2019–2020).
Served as on-site assistant to project managers at COVID-19 mass care sites (2021–2022).
Handled office manager duties at IEM: deliveries, conference supplies, flight booking, and help with onboarding and offboarding (2019–2024).
interview_questions: What do you know about ICAP, and why does this role interest you?
Tell us about a time you juggled several deadlines and stakeholders on a project.
How would you handle a frustrated student, partner, or member of the public?
What tools have you used to track program activities and report progress?
watch_outs: The posting has no description or salary, so you can't verify fit or pay until you see the full listing.
It is open until filled, so it could close without notice. Apply soon.
A degree may be required; his M.A. (George Mason, 2016) covers a general degree requirement.
If ICAP is a specialized academic or research program, it may be less related to your policy and emergency-management interests.
